_what: Figures for rccl-atomics-hostcall.html, extracted from docs/root-cause.md.

chain.link: The root port above the GPU advertises no 32/64-bit AtomicOp completer support
chain.evidence: guest lspci -vvs 00:1c.0 → AtomicOpsCap: Routing- 32bit- 64bit-, the emulated pcie-root-port. Two bits matter here and are easy to conflate: completion on the root port, routing on any switch port in between. This repository's own host reports Routing- 32bit+ 64bit+ on all eight root ports and does pass: amdgpu bound these same cards on the host across five boots and never emitted the message, while in the guest it emits it for both GPUs at every boot. The passthrough layer removes the capability, not the Zen 1 silicon

guest dmesg: amdgpu 0000:01:00.0: PCIE atomic ops is not supported (every GPU). pci_enable_atomic_ops_to_root() requires COMP32+COMP64 at the root port and AtomicOp routing on each switch port below it; the emulated root port carries neither completer bit

chain.link: → ROCr cannot build a hostcall buffer
chain.evidence: AMD_LOG_LEVEL=4 at the exact failure: rocvirtual.cpp:4208 Pcie atomics not enabled, hostcall not supported → 4636 AQL dispatch failed! → hipErrorIllegalState. Hostcall's ring signalling depends on atomics

chain.link: → any kernel needing hostcall is refused
chain.evidence: diagnose/hipgate3.cpp: identical launch path, two kernels. Plain kernel passes; kernel with device printf (which requires hostcall) fails with the exact production error

llvm-readelf --notes on the device image: every ncclDevKernel_Generic carries hidden_hostcall_buffer. Source: device-side assert() throughout src/device/ links __assert_fail; ENABLE_COLLTRACE adds device printf → __ockl_fprintf

ruled_out.how: Raised 16 G → 22 G, identical signature; no OOM in dmesg, headroom at crash
Two public bare-metal reports are single-NUMA desktops (7800X3D, 13900K) and reproduce

independently reproduced on bare metal with IOMMU entirely disabled, by @adderek in ROCm#6520: 2× RX 7900 XTX on a B550 board, same failure, same fix. Their machine has one affected GPU (chipset-attached) and one healthy one (CPU-direct)
0.19.1 and 0.23 fail, 0.11.2 passes — it is only the caller
Our own b38 built from source still failed — because our build did not get NDEBUG to the device pass either. The variable is hostcall, not version
Read the source: string check only, warns but does not gate
Read the source: both generations use an ordinary DisableTiming event
diagnose/hipgate.cpp issues the exact hipExtLaunchKernel + completion-event form, 4 KB kernarg, cross-stream wait, fine-grained host memory — all pass on 7.14
diagnose/hipgate2.cpp, 0 → 64 KB, all pass (over-limit returns a correctly different error)

diagnose/sweep.sh: 11 combinations of NCCL_P2P_DISABLE, HSA_ENABLE_SDMA, NCCL_SHM_DISABLE, NCCL_CUMEM_ENABLE, HSA_FORCE_FINE_GRAIN_PCIE, GPU_MAX_HW_QUEUES, AMD_SERIALIZE_KERNEL — signature unchanged in all

ruled_out.hypothesis: Pipeline parallel instead of tensor parallel
ruled_out.how: diagnose/ar_p2p.py: ncclSend/Recv kernels need hostcall too, same crash
The whole of §1, and decisively hipgate3.cpp
